references.text: Earlier in the chapter, John the Baptist testifies that Jesus is the one who "comes after" him but was before him: [ref:Joh 1:15|John 1:15]. This is the same theme of the one who comes after John.
John repeats this same testimony shortly afterward in [ref:Joh 1:30|John 1:30], where he again points to the one who comes after him and was before him.
In [ref:Matt 3:11|Matthew 3:11], John the Baptist says almost identical words: he is not worthy to carry the sandals of the one who comes after him. Parallel passage in the Synoptics.
In [ref:Mark 1:7|Mark 1:7], John says that one will come after him who is stronger, and that he is not worthy to bend down and untie the straps of his sandals – an almost word-for-word parallel.
Luke records the same statement in [ref:Luk 3:16|Luke 3:16], where John says he is not worthy to untie the sandal strap of the one who comes after him.

Paul quotes the words of John the Baptist in his speech at Antioch: [ref:Apg 13:25|Acts 13:25] – "I am not the one you think I am. But after me comes one whom I am not worthy to untie the sandals of."
John the Baptist later repeats that he was sent ahead for Christ, and that Christ must increase but he himself must decrease – [ref:Joh 3:28-30|John 3:28–30]. This confirms John’s subordinate role.

The prophecy in [ref:Jes 40:3|Isaiah 40:3] about the voice crying out in the wilderness and making a way for the Lord is the background for John the Baptist’s ministry as the forerunner of the Messiah.

In [ref:Mal 3:1|Malachi 3:1], it is promised that God will send his messenger ahead to prepare the way. John the Baptist is the fulfillment of this prophecy as the one who goes before the coming Messiah.
